natural_experiments.what: Same month, same qualified wallets, matches under two venue regimes (regime is per match). Net / gross 30 s markout per print, match-clustered bootstrap CI of the difference (b - a). IS prints only.

composition.what: Shift-share of the fall in the fast tier's net edge between period A (Dec 2025 - Apr 2026, 3 s delay) and period B (Jun - Aug 2026 IS part, 1 s delay). Incumbents = wallets first qualified for a month up to Apr 2026; entrants = first qualified from May 2026. delta net = fee part + incumbents' gross change + entrant dilution (exact identity, because in A every print is an incumbent's).

definitions.incumbents: wallets first qualified (walk-forward) for a month up to Apr 2026
definitions.first4: the 4 wallets qualified for Dec 2025 (the paper's 'fast tier grew from 4')
definitions.entrants: wallets first qualified from May 2026 on
definitions.survivorship: a wallet that stops trading simply drops out of a month; no wallet is picked on the months it is scored on (walk-forward)

profit.what: Fast-tier $ P&L per month at the 30 s mark after fees (sum of shares x net markout), IS prints. Dec 2025 is left out of the fits (17 catalogue matches that month, a coverage artefact).
profit.kappa_note: kappa = exact $ P&L / (print-mean edge x $ volume). It is ~2 because a dollar buys ~2 shares at ~50c and larger prints earn more per share; it moves month to month, so the proxy is a rough guide for the OOS months only.

step_model_may2026.label: WLS of net edge on a May-2026 step (weights = matches); compares with the straight line on AICc
step_model_may2026.reading: the step fits at least as well as the line (lower AICc); with the step in, no trend is left, so on this reading the edge is not heading to zero at any measurable pace

reading.who_pays: The fast tier hits resting quotes that still show the pre-point price, so the maker on the other side loses the gross markout (about 1.5c a share in Jun-Aug 2026). The venue keeps the taker fee (1.02c a share on 1 s / 5% prints in Jul 2026), and other takers trading in the same 0-3 s lose 0.5-1.9c a share.
reading.what_the_decline_is: The net edge fell 0.16c a month (WLS, 11 calendar months, CI -0.25 to -0.06). Over the same months the fee rose +0.13c a month while the gross edge moved -0.02c a month (CI -0.12 to +0.07; IS-only exact -0.04, CI -0.19 to +0.11). From Dec-Apr to Jun-Aug the net edge fell 0.85c: 0.54c is the fee, 0.40c is weaker wallets joining, and the early wallets' own gross edge moved +0.08c.
reading.venue_rules: Within May 2026, the same wallets earned +0.14c (CI -0.04 to +0.32) more on 1 s-hold matches than on 3 s ones, so the shorter hold did not hurt them. Within Jul 2026, 5%-fee matches paid -0.29c (CI -0.47 to -0.11) net with the same gross (difference +0.11c, CI -0.06 to +0.28): the fee is passed straight through. The best single break in the net series is May 2026; a step there (AICc -24.3) fits at least as well as a straight line (-21.1) and leaves a trend of -0.05c a month (CI -0.20 to +0.09).
reading.why_it_can_persist: Someone always sees the point before the book reprices (court, broadcast and data-feed delays are physical) and the 1 s hold only narrows that window. Wallets already fast by Apr 2026 kept their gross edge (+0.07c a month, CI -0.10 to +0.23) while the field grew from 4 to 131 wallets; the first four slipped 0.06c a month (CI -0.17 to +0.06, not significant).
reading.what_kills_it: (1) A higher fee: the fast tier's gross edge covers a taker fee of up to 8.4% (today 5%). (2) A longer taker hold or makers on a faster official feed, which would remove the stale quotes. (3) More entrants: the monthly pool grew with wallets at elasticity 0.53 (CI 0.21 to 0.85), so each wallet's share fell at -0.47 (CI -0.79 to -0.15) per 1% more wallets, from about $1.7k a month in Jan-May 2026 to about $0.4k in Aug.
reading.for_an_entrant: The number that matters is the pool and one wallet's share of it, not the average edge per share. The pool has been flat since May 2026 while wallets kept arriving.
reading.projection: A straight line says zero in 3.3 months after Sep 2026 (Fieller CI 0.6 to 12.8); a constant % decline says 12% less a month (half-life 5.2 months, CI 3.4 to 11.1); the step model says flat at 0.73c. The data cannot tell these apart, and only the line reaches zero.
